title: Part 1.III — Scope and Reduction
role: The longest Part 1 chapter (68 pp.) and the source of two of Burke's most dissertation-portable methodological constructs: the *representative anecdote* (the small case that condenses an entire pattern of motivation and serves as the scaled-down model for analysis) and *circumference* (the scope of scene chosen by an analyst — a town, a nation, an epoch, the cosmos — which determines what motives become visible). The chapter develops Act as the locus of motives (book pp.64-69), works through the way of creation in cosmological systems, and extends to a long case study of monetary reduction (the way 'money as God-term' in capitalist motive-vocabularies substitutes a quantitative measure for qualitative motive). Phase 3 will mine this chapter for the representative-anecdote and circumference methodological apparatus as transferable instruments for the dissertation's game-user-motive-analysis.
